# Console commands

The application has a text console on the UART of the board (how to open it: [build and flash, step 8](../guide/build-and-flash.md#step-8-the-console)). This page lists every command the neXtBSW application can register, with its syntax, what it does and in which build it exists. It is **generated** from the sources: the command registration and help texts in the C++ code, the CMake conditions and build options, the module manifests, the projects and the board READMEs. A test fails as soon as page and sources disagree. `help` on the console shows what the running build really contains.

## How to read this page

- **Syntax** - `<group> <command> [parameters]`. Parameters are shown where the help text states them (`param: ...` or `Usage: ...`); a command without them may still take parameters - the purpose column then says so in the words of its help text. `help <group>` prints the commands of one group.
- **Available** - the conditions under which the group is built in: the family port it belongs to, the module a project must use, a `PLATFORM_SUPPORT_*` switch derived from the project and its board (ARCH-58), a CMake build option for test builds. *Only in* adds conditions of a single command. *Always* means: in every build of the application.
- **Per-device groups** - modules with `console: instance` in their manifest register one group per board device they serve; its name is the device's `console` parameter in `project.yaml`. They are listed as `<name>`, with the names the projects in this repository use in the [project table](#projects).
- **Board rule** - the command may only be used with a person at the board. The mark comes from the help text, which ends in the marker “(board rule)” (SYS-17; the earlier wordings “only with the user at the board”, “board rules apply” still count, but `tools/docgen --gaps` reports them), or from the list “Only with a person at the board:” in the README of a board. The marker is what a person at the console sees in `help`, so every command in a board's list should carry it. Whether a command is dangerous depends on how the board is wired, so the board README is the authority; an unmarked command is not declared safe.

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `csec status` | CSEc, FlexRAM, FCSESTAT, watchdogs, staged M1..M3, last command |  |  |
| `m1` | `csec m1 <32 hex>` | stage M1 (param: &lt;32 hex>, from tools/csec load-master) |  |  |
| `m2` | `csec m2 <64 hex>` | stage M2 (param: &lt;64 hex>) |  |  |
| `m3` | `csec m3 <32 hex>` | stage M3 (param: &lt;32 hex>) |  |  |
| `loadkey` | `csec loadkey LOADKEY-MASTER-ECU-KEY` | IRREVERSIBLE: load the MASTER_ECU_KEY into its empty slot (param: LOADKEY-MASTER-ECU-KEY) (board rule) |  | yes (help text) |
| `rng` | `csec rng` | reset, then INIT_RNG at the start before the safety task (needed once per reset) (board rule) |  | yes (help text) |
| `challenge` | `csec challenge` | GET_ID and DBG_CHAL: UID, CHALLENGE, word for dbgauth (board rule) |  | yes (help text) |
| `dbgauth` | `csec dbgauth <32 hex> DBGAUTH-XXXXXXXX` | IRREVERSIBLE: erase all keys and the partition (param: &lt;32 hex> DBGAUTH-XXXXXXXX) (board rule) |  | yes (help text) |

### `dflash` - data flash areas (NVM-23, test build)

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; build option `-DNX_DFLASH_COMMAND=ON` (default OFF); `NX_DFLASH_AREA_COUNT > 0` (preprocessor macro); `defined(NX_DFLASH_AREA_COUNT)` (preprocessor macro)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | `dflash show` | chip, driver, areas, job |  |  |
| `read` | `dflash read <area> <offset> <length up to 64>` | read through read() (param: &lt;area> &lt;offset> &lt;length up to 64>) |  |  |
| `erase` | `dflash erase <area>` | erase every sector of an area (param: &lt;area>) |  |  |

<a id="c-inject"></a>

### `inject` - Safety fault injection, ends in a safety reset (test build only)

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; build option `-DNX_SAFETY_FAULT_INJECTION_COMMAND=ON` (default OFF)
- **Defined in:** [`SafetyFaultInjectionCommand.cpp`](../../platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/integration/SafetyFaultInjectionCommand.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `SafetyFaultInjectionCommand`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deadman` | `inject deadman [tval\|mier\|dbgen\|prio]` | falsify the LPIT deadman channel (param: [tval\|mier\|dbgen\|prio], default tval) - DEADMAN_CONFIGURATION_ERROR |  |  |
| `wdogint` | `inject wdogint` | clear WDOG_CS[INT] while running - SAFE_WATCHDOG_CONFIGURATION_ERROR fields 0x2 |  |  |
| `mspuse` | `inject mspuse` | no fault: high-water mark of the interrupt stack since start (fill pattern, SYS-97) |  |  |
| `mspoverflow` | `inject mspoverflow` | move the interrupt stack pointer onto its guard and pend SysTick - hard fault, interrupt stack overflow |  |  |

<a id="c-safety"></a>

### `safety` - Commands to test safety features

- **Available:** `PLATFORM_SUPPORT_IO`, derived from project and board (on in `buildtest_s32k148_min`, `evalboard_s32k144_charge`, `evalboard_s32k144_demo`, `nucleo_f446re_demo`, `s32k116evb_minimal`); build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF); `!defined(NX_PRODUCT_BUILD)` (preprocessor macro); with console (`NX_CONSOLE`)
- **Defined in:** [`SafetyCommand.cpp`](../../ecu/consoleCommands/src/safety/console/SafetyCommand.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `SafetyCommand`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mpu` | `safety mpu` | Write to protected memory (enforce MPU violation) |  |  |
| `wdg` | `safety wdg` | Enter infinite loop (enforce watchdog reset) |  |  |
| `prt` | `safety prt` | Write to protected register (has no effect) |  |  |
| `dst` | `safety dst` | Disable safety test pin (enter safe state) |  |  |
| `est` | `safety est` | Re-enable safety test pin (leave safe state) |  |  |

<a id="c-sbc"></a>

### `sbc` - UJA113x system basis chip

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; module [`sbcUja113x`](modules.md#m-sbcuja113x)
- **Defined in:** [`SbcSystem.cpp`](../../platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/systems/SbcSystem.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `SbcSystem::Command`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `sbc status` | state, supply, transceiver, counters, INTN pins |  |  |
| `dump` | `sbc dump` | read all documented registers |  |  |
| `read` | `sbc read <address>` | read register (param: &lt;address>) |  |  |
| `write` | `sbc write <address> <value>` | write register (param: &lt;address> &lt;value>), not 0x00/0x01/MTPNV | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |
| `sleep` | `sbc sleep` | enter SBC Sleep, MCU supply off, wake-up by CAN (board rule) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) | yes (help text); yes on `evalboard_s32k144` (not published, available on request) as `sbc sleep` |
| `failstart` | `sbc failstart` | reset now and in the next &lt;n> (0..3) starts before the SBC start, JP1 test (board rule) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) | yes (help text); yes on `evalboard_s32k144` (not published, available on request) as `sbc failstart <n>` |
| `pn` | `sbc pn` | arm: write CAN wake-up frame registers (0x20, 0x26..0x2F, 0x68..0x6F) without Sleep | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |
| `standby` | `sbc standby` | SBC Standby, V1 on, CAN offline, until a wake-up or &lt;ms> (100..600000) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |

<a id="c-shortlock"></a>

### `shortlock` - SYS-172 lock time of the safe state selection (test build only)

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; build option `-DNX_SHORT_LOCK_MEASURE_COMMAND=ON` (default OFF); `TARGET nxSafeOutputSelection`
- **Defined in:** [`ShortLockMeasureCommand.cpp`](../../platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/systems/ShortLockMeasureCommand.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `ShortLockMeasureCommand`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | `shortlock show` | count, last and longest lock per call site in cycles and ns |  |  |
| `reset` | `shortlock reset` | clear the figures |  |  |
| `select` | `shortlock select <state 0\|1\|2> [<count 1..1000>] [<group>]` | call nxSafeStateSelect (param: &lt;state 0\|1\|2> [&lt;count 1..1000>] [&lt;group>], default 1 0) |  |  |
| `block` | `shortlock block [<group>]` | call nxSafeStateBlockShort (param: [&lt;group>], default 0) - short removed until power-on |  |  |

<a id="c-shutdownhang"></a>

### `shutdownhang` - SYS-173 test: level-2 component hangs in its next shutdown (test build only)

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; build option `-DNX_SHUTDOWN_HANG_COMMAND=ON` (default OFF)
- **Defined in:** [`ShutdownHangCommand.cpp`](../../platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/integration/ShutdownHangCommand.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `ShutdownHangCommand`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `arm` | `shutdownhang arm [<release_ms>]` | hang in the next shutdown, then "ecu sleep" (param: [&lt;release_ms>], default 30000, 0 = never) |  |  |
| `disarm` | `shutdownhang disarm` | no hang; a running hang ends now and the shutdown goes on |  |  |
| `show` | `shutdownhang show` | armed, hanging, time since the hang began |  |  |

<a id="c-stats"></a>

### `stats` - lifecycle statistics command

- **Available:** in every application
- **Defined in:** [`StatisticsCommand.cpp`](../../ecu/consoleCommands/src/lifecycle/console/StatisticsCommand.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `StatisticsCommand`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `stats cpu` | prints CPU statistics |  |  |
| `stack` | `stats stack` | prints stack statistics |  |  |
| `all` | `stats all` | prints all statistics |  |  |

## Per-device command groups

<a id="c-instance-bccmc33771"></a>

### per device of module `bccMc33771` (after R1) (name from the project, default `bcc`)

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; module [`bccMc33771`](modules.md#m-bccmc33771)
- **Name:** the parameter `console` of each device the module serves (`project.yaml`, `modules.<device>.console`), the help text is set with it; see [project description](project.md) and [modules](modules.md#m-bccmc33771)
- **Defined in:** `CellMonitorSystem.cpp` (not published, available on request) (neXtBSW, class `CellMonitorSystem::Command`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `<bcc> status` | state, faults, balancing, counters |  |  |
| `cells` | `<bcc> cells` | last measurement: cells, stack, inputs, IC temperature, current |  |  |
| `dump` | `<bcc> dump` | read configuration and status registers |  |  |
| `read` | `<bcc> read <address>` | read register (param: &lt;address>) |  |  |
| `write` | `<bcc> write <address> <value>` | write a fault status register, 0 clears (param: &lt;address> &lt;value>) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |
| `clear` | `<bcc> clear` | clear latched faults and device fault registers | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |
| `stop` | `<bcc> stop` | switch cell balancing off |  |  |

<a id="c-instance-gdtmc6200"></a>

### per device of module `gdTmc6200` (after R1) (name from the project, default `gd`)

- **Available:** family `s32k1xx`; module [`gdTmc6200`](modules.md#m-gdtmc6200)
- **Name:** the parameter `console` of each device the module serves (`project.yaml`, `modules.<device>.console`), the help text is set with it; see [project description](project.md) and [modules](modules.md#m-gdtmc6200)
- **Defined in:** [`GateDriverSystem.cpp`](../../platforms/s32k1xx/port/main/src/systems/GateDriverSystem.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `GateDriverSystem::Command`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `<gd> status` | state, faults, GSTAT/IOIN, counters |  |  |
| `dump` | `<gd> dump` | read all documented registers |  |  |
| `read` | `<gd> read <address>` | read register (param: &lt;address>) |  |  |
| `write` | `<gd> write <address> <value>` | write GCONF/GSTAT/SHORT_CONF/DRV_CONF (param: &lt;address> &lt;value>), only with DRV_EN off | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |
| `clear` | `<gd> clear` | clear latched faults and GSTAT flags (DRV_EN stays off) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |
| `off` | `<gd> off` | DRV_EN off |  |  |
| `enable` | `<gd> enable` | TEST BUILD: DRV_EN on through the driver, only disabled, no faults (board rule) | build option `-DNX_GD_ENABLE_COMMAND=ON` (default OFF) | yes (help text) |

<a id="c-instance-highsideswitch"></a>

### per device of module `highSideSwitch` (name from the project, no default)

- **Available:** module [`highSideSwitch`](modules.md#m-highsideswitch)
- **Name:** the parameter `console` of each device the module serves (`project.yaml`, `modules.<device>.console`), the help text is set with it; see [project description](project.md) and [modules](modules.md#m-highsideswitch)
- **Defined in:** [`HighSideSwitchSystem.cpp`](../../libs/bsw/highSideSwitch/src/highSideSwitch/HighSideSwitchSystem.cpp) (neXtBSW, class `HighSideSwitchSystem::Command`)

| Command | Syntax | Purpose | Only in | Board rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `<name> status` | state, fault, load current, IS raw value, thresholds, counters |  |  |
| `on` | `<name> on` | switch on, load supply (board rule) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) | yes (help text); yes on `evalboard_s32k144` (not published, available on request) as `kl30b on` |
| `off` | `<name> off` | switch off |  |  |
| `reset` | `<name> reset` | clear a latched overcurrent/diagnosis fault (stays off) | build option `-DNX_PRODUCT_BUILD=OFF` (default OFF) |  |

## Board rules

- `evalboard_s32k144` (not published, available on request): `sbc sleep`, `ecu sleep`, `sbc failstart <n>`, `kl30b on` are console commands of its projects (marked above); also listed there, not a console command of its projects: `canflash blupdate`, `MOT1_GD_DRV_EN`.
